source_spans.locator: Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published p.185, Abstract and opening: low-demand situations can benefit from added challenge whereas extremely high-demand situations can benefit from reduced load

Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published pp.186-187, task-complexity and processing-capacity discussion: functional demand varies with task and performer experience; learning is distinguished from acquisition performance by later test performance; added demands may compete for limited processing capacity

Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published pp.193-194, feedback discussion and summary: demand-increasing feedback schedules can degrade acquisition/learning of higher-demand tasks, whereas frequent or blocked feedback can facilitate them

Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published pp.195-196, Physical Assistance: assistance can reduce task demands to a manageable level and can transfer to later unassisted performance, but the benefit is task-dependent rather than universal

Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published pp.198-204, attentional-focus and observational-practice sections: some practice conditions reduce attentional, control, or execution demands and can improve later performance on demanding tasks

Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2), published pp.206-207, Task Difficulty as a Mediating Factor and final synthesis: effects can vary with task difficulty and practice stage; low-demand situations favor added load/challenge, whereas extremely high-demand acquisition favors load reduction

conditions: training situations spanning low to extremely high cognitive, attentional, and motor demands
functional demand varies with task characteristics, performer experience, and stage of practice
population: human learners and performers of motor tasks
task: motor tasks differing in functional demand, degrees of freedom, coordination requirements, and time needed to reach stable performance
temporal_scope: during acquisition, with learning distinguished from immediate practice performance by later retention, transfer, or test performance where available
effects of a practice manipulation may change as experience accumulates

nodes.description: current cognitive, attentional, and motor demand of the training situation
performer expertise or stage of practice that can alter the functional demand of a task and the effect of practice conditions
degree to which current task and practice demands load or overload the performer's limited processing resources
practice manipulation that adds cognitive effort, processing demand, or challenge
practice manipulation that reduces otherwise excessive cognitive, attentional, control, or execution demands
later retention, transfer, or other test condition used where available to distinguish learning from immediate acquisition performance
performance on a later assessment used as evidence about what was learned during practice

relations.description: functional task difficulty is relative to performer experience and to the degree that current demands load available processing resources
the review-level synthesis favors added challenge for learning when the current training situation imposes relatively low demands
the review-level synthesis favors demand reduction for learning when acquisition already imposes extremely high demands
the effect of a practice condition may change across practice as functional task demands change
later retention, transfer, or test performance is used where available to assess learning rather than equating immediate acquisition performance with learning
